description: Labeled cases for failure_scan.py's machine-decidable modes (M1/M3/M5/M6/M7). Negatives carry the near-miss shapes each tell must NOT fire on — an ordinary metric value, a cited surprise, a corroborated hyperparameter — because a detector is only as good as what it declines to flag. M2 (delegated) and M4 (not automated) emit no findings by design and are covered by unit tests, not here.

mutations.breaks: A reported standard deviation of exactly 0.00 stops being flagged as the impossible-result tell it is.
An uncorroborated 'surprisingly' stops being flagged — the HARKing tell that mode exists for.
The suspicious-exact-metric set is emptied, so a reported accuracy of exactly 1 stops being questioned.
A grouped record count reads as a decimal, so it is treated as a measurement and reported as an own result with no artefact behind it — while the artefact holding the integer sits in analysis/.

A metric value inside a sentence that cites a source is scored as this paper's own result, so a review that REPORTS someone else's implausible 1.0 — and diagnoses the leakage in the next clause — is flagged for doing its job.

The backing-saturation measure stops downgrading a meaningless CLEAR. This is the defect it was written for: on a real review the pool backed 100% of two-decimal values and M3 reported CLEAR over a paragraph produced by no script at all.
